pr_title: drivers: flash: spi_nor: add SFDP support
pr_body:
Implementation for #25958 with demonstration with existing SPI NOR driver and an example.

This reworks the `jedec,spi-nor` common bindings to allow describing device properties with the Basic Flash Parameters table from the [JESD216](https://www.jedec.org/standards-documents/docs/jesd216b) Serial Flash Discoverable Parameters capability.

A jesd216 module is added in drivers/flash that defines constants and data structures related to SFDP processing and provides helper functions to extract data.  Optionally this API can be exposed to applications, which enables a sample application that displays the supported features of a connected device and dumps the devicetree property settings required to support it.  Because the API is unlikely to be used generally the header documentation is not tagged for generating user documentation.

The SPI NOR driver is updated to use the jesd216 data from a BFP structure. This currently supports additional erase sizes and non-standard page sizes, but with the infrastructure in place can be extended to support 4-byte addressing, sleeping rather than busy-waiting for operation completion, and other features.  Deep-power-down may be automatically supported, though initial investigation suggests the BFP doesn't provide sufficient information on entry/exit timing.

The SPI NOR driver is updated to support specifying flash parameters through several mechanisms:
* `CONFIG_SPI_NOR_SFDP_MINIMAL` validates the JEDEC ID and provides size from devicetree.  It supports only the standard erase types and page sizes.
* `CONFIG_SPI_NOR_SFDP_DEVICETREE` takes the BFP content from the devicetree node.  It supports any runtime-detectable feature without the overhead of reading the device at runtime.
* `CONFIG_SPI_NOR_SFDP_RUNTIME` reads the BFP content at runtime.  This allows the same firmware to support any underlying JESD216-compatible flash device.

Related issues and PRs
* Closes #25958
* Supersedes #23658
* Supports STM32 QSPI #25806
* Supports NXP iMX QSPI #25669 (superseding #15364)

issue_context.title: Concept Overview for improving support for serial flash devices via SPI and QSPI
issue_context.body:
It's becoming increasingly clear that the old theory that we should provide SPI NOR flash parameters via devicetree is becoming unsustainable; cf  #23322, #22965, and some slack conversations about newer chips with much larger sizes.  That original policy was based on a perception that runtime extraction of device parameters was too costly in flash and RAM.

While one approach is prototyped in #25806 I was looking for something that's a little more comprehensive, including being prepared to support other parameter blocks.  This issue provides a retroactive RFC for how to support a wider range of serial flash devices by using the JEDEC Serial Flash Discoverable Parameters tables that can be read from JESD216-compatible devices, including most SPI NOR serial flashes supported by the Zephyr spi-nor flash driver and other in-tree and pending flash interfaces (primarily QSPI).

The general concept is:

* Provide data structures and decoders that operate on JESD216 headers and parameter tables.
* Use [`jedec,spi-nor`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/mtd/jedec%2Cspi-nor.txt) as the compatible, with an extension to define the SFDP Basic Flash Parameters via an `sfdp-bfp` property for cases where runtime determination of characteristics is not desired.
* Follow Linux examples ([stm32](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/spi/st%2Cstm32-qspi.yaml), [freescale](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/spi/spi-fsl-qspi.txt)) for describing controllers.  Note that these bindings may be associated with Zephyr flash devices rather than SPI devices, and that the child nodes should be `jedec,spi-nor` compatibles (with additional properties using a more specific compatible that extends `jedec,spi-nor`).
* Provide a way to re-use in utility applications the SFDP and JEDEC ID functions implemented by specific drivers.  A specific application is one that reads a device and generates the `sfdp-bfp` and `jedec-id` property values.
* Where the current bindings provide parameters that can be obtained from SFDP the corresponding properties should be deprecated/removed and the SFDP encodings used.
* Where driver-specific devicetree properties are required those may be added via a compatible that extends the `jedec-spi-common.yaml` binding set.

The information from SFDP enables a lot of other potential enhancements including better control of deep power down and use of timing information to reduce time spent busy-waiting for operations to complete.

These APIs and functionality are prototoyped in #25851, currently only for the legacy SPI NOR driver.  As we identify functional commonalities, such as identifying erase commands for a specific offset and span, these can be pulled out into a shared implementation for use by specific drivers.
comments:
> * Use [`jedec,spi-nor`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/mtd/jedec%2Cspi-nor.txt) as the compatible, with an extension to define the SFDP Basic Flash Parameters via an `sfdp-bfp` property for cases where runtime determination of characteristics is not desired.

The device tree specification states:
_The compatible property value consists of one or more strings that define the specific programming model for the device. This list of strings should be used by a client program for device driver selection. The property value consists of a concatenated list of null terminated strings, from most specific to most general. They allow a device to express its compatibility with a family of similar devices, potentially allowing a single device driver to match against several devices._

The compatible property is used to associate DTS node with the device driver. While we don't use this mechanism in Zephyr (yet), we shouldn't purposefully violate the specification. Using `compatible = "jedec,spi-nor"` for flash devices attached to QSPI controller would be fine if the drivers/flash/spi_nor.c was able to handle QSPI devices.

In Linux the spi-nor driver is able to control both SPI and QSPI flash devices and they consistently use jedec,spi-nor compatible for the flash nodes.

> The compatible property is used to associate DTS node with the device driver. While we don't use this mechanism in Zephyr (yet), we shouldn't purposefully violate the specification. Using `compatible = "jedec,spi-nor"` for flash devices attached to QSPI controller would be fine if the drivers/flash/spi_nor.c was able to handle QSPI devices.
> 
> In Linux the spi-nor driver is able to control both SPI and QSPI flash devices and they consistently use jedec,spi-nor compatible for the flash nodes.

That isn't how I understand what Linux does.  In the [stm32](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/spi/st%2Cstm32-qspi.yaml) and [freescale](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/spi/spi-fsl-qspi.txt) it isn't the generic spi-nor driver that is used for those controllers.  That's exactly the situation we have in Zephyr.

Linux is [pretty clear](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/mtd/jedec%2Cspi-nor.txt#L9) that *a* compatible for the flash memory itself, regardless of its controller, should be `jedec,spi-nor`.  (A more specific compatible can be added if additional properties are required.)

Dev-review (Jun 4, 2020): Discussed how we should represent this in DTS, and semantic differences about programming model vs driver.  For now we should have at least `jedec,spi-nor` on any flash device node that conforms to that programming model.  In practice the combination of the `jedec,spi-nor` node and its parent are what really tell us how or which driver should come into play.
We need to look at implementing improvements on DT_CHILD_* related to this functionality.

How does this relate to the chosen nodes in Zephyr?
Do we need both `zephyr, flash` and `zephyr, flash-controller`?

Personally I've never knowingly made use of either of those chosen properties.

At least one use of them in the tree seems to be wrong, as it assumes a partition is on the "chosen" controller, which is unreliable.  The proper controller can be found from the partition node itself (now, at least, maybe it couldn't in legacy devicetree).

Yes, exactly. This caused much confusion when I started to look at this. If I remember correctly, it is MCUBOOT that uses the `zephyr, flash-controller` part. It should probably be changed to grab the information it needs through the partitions instead, as it won't need to do anything to the controller itself I guess.

review_comments: The `dw & BIT_MASK(31)` is expected to be >=32. Assertion here?

Thanks for the review.  I've tweaked it a bit for the other two comments, but I don't think this is worth doing: it's unlikely to happen with real devices, and if somebody screws up a devicetree table it'll probably be obvious without depending on somebody enabling asserts to detect it.
